attributes.name: Height
attributes.description: The height from the table, or thickness, of the computer while closed. This includes the keyboard dock on detachable laptops.

attributes.name: Depth
attributes.description: The depth, from the front edge to the back hinge, of the computer while closed. This includes the keyboard dock for detachable laptops.

attributes.name: Width
attributes.description: The width of the computer while closed. This includes the keyboard dock of detachable laptops.

attributes.name: Thin and light
attributes.description: Based on weight and thickness. This includes laptops that may be labeled "Ultrabook," "Sleekbook," "Thin and light," and "Ultrathin," among other terms.

attributes.name: Warranty length
attributes.description: The length in months of the manufacturer's standard warranty.

attributes.name: Tech support length
attributes.description: The length in months of the manufacturer's free technical support by telephone.

attributes.name: Battery capacity
attributes.description: The total energy contained in the battery, expressed in Watt-hours. A larger capacity battery will deliver longer battery life, but will add weight and sometimes will extend beyond the edge of the laptop.

attributes.name: Comes in S Mode
attributes.description: Windows computers that come in S Mode can only run apps from the Microsoft Store. This is one way to ensure system security and stability. They can be switched out of S Mode for free, allowing them to run third-party applications. We test computers switched out of S Mode.

attributes.name: Suitable for gaming
attributes.description: All systems can play casual games such as solitaire and Angry Birds. Systems designated as suitable for gaming are more powerful and can play modern mainstream and intensive 3D video games with a frame rate and visual effects that does not make the game stop or stutter.

attributes.name: Blu-ray or DVD
attributes.description: Has either a Blu-Ray drive (B), which lets you watch Blu-Ray movies and read/write to CDs and DVDs, or a DVD drive (D), which lets you read/write to CDs and DVDs. Some computers have no optical drive installed (—).

attributes.name: Memory-card reader
attributes.description: At least one flash memory-card slot (CF, SD, XD, MS, etc.)

attributes.name: Facial recognition
attributes.description: Webcam can be set to scan your face for secure log-in.

attributes.name: Fingerprint reader
attributes.description: A biometric fingerprint reader for logging into your PC.

attributes.name: WiFi type
attributes.description: The type of built-in 802.11 wireless networking supported. Computers with 802.11n also support 802.11g routers. Some models with 802.11n also support the 5GHz "high band," a standard suitable for apartments and other crowded areas.

attributes.name: Thunderbolt port
attributes.description: Has a Thunderbolt port for connecting peripherals such as an external hard drive. This includes ports that may be on the keyboard dock of detachable laptops. Thunderbolt is a high-speed port that can connect to DVI, HDMI and VGA through the use of adapters. Thunderbolt 3 is the newest version that supports faster speeds.

attributes.name: Digital video out
attributes.description: Has an HDMI, DisplayPort, or Thunderbolt video output for sending a digital video signal to a computer monitor or HDTV.

attributes.name: Number of USB ports
attributes.description: Number of USB ports for printers, flash drives, or other peripherals. This includes ports that may be on the keyboard dock of detachable laptops.

attributes.name: Gigabit Ethernet
attributes.description: Support for 1,000 Mb/s networking.

attributes.name: HDMI output
attributes.description: An HDMI out port for sending a digital video/audio signal to a computer monitor or HDTV.

ownerSatisfaction.infoText: Owner satisfaction ratings are based on the proportion of members who are extremely likely to recommend their laptop to their friends and family.

expertReview.summary: A 14.0-inch convertible laptop tested with Windows 10 Home, an Intel Core i5-1035G1 1GHz processor, 8GB of memory, Intel UHD Graphics graphics, a touchscreen, and a 256GB solid-state drive.
expertReview.bottomLine: The Acer Spin 3 is a 14-inch laptop with a touchscreen display. Performance speeds are Very Good for complex productivity work, but you might notice a slowdown during more demanding video games or graphical tasks. Battery life is average for its size, at just over 11 hours in web browsing tests.
expertReview.highs:
• Touchscreen provides a convenient way to navigate and interact
• Comes with a fast, more efficient solid-state drive
• Has a fingerprint reader
expertReview.lows:
• Compared to typical hard drives, this solid-state drive provides less storage space
• No optical drive
expertReview.description:
The Acer Spin 3 SP314-54N-58Q7 is a 14-inch convertible laptop with a screen resolution of 1920 x 1080. It has 8GB of memory and a 256GB solid-state drive. It has an Intel Core i5-1035G1 1GHz processor and an integrated Intel UHD Graphics. It lacks an optical drive for burning CDs or DVDs. It was tested with Windows 10 Home installed.

It has a touch screen, 2 full-size, 1 type-C USB ports built-in on the laptop. Video outputs include: an HDMI full-size port, supporting Thunderbolt 3 (40 Gbps) and DisplayPort over USB-C. It supports WiFi 5 (802.11ac), so it's compatible with high-speed routers. It also supports WiFi 6 (802.11ax), which provides faster and more dependable High Efficiency Wireless, but you'll need a compatible router to see the faster speeds. It has a 0.9MP webcam for video conferencing. There is a built-in slot holder for the stylus. It comes with a carrying case.

The Acer Spin 3 SP314-54N-58Q7 measures 12.8 inches wide by 9.1 inches deep by 0.7 inches high, and it weighs 3.3 lbs. It's backed by a 12-month warranty, with 12 months of free tech support over telephone.
expertReview.review:
Performance: Overall this laptop's performance was only Fair, well below that of many models but still good enough for routine tasks like email, word processing and web browsing. Compared to other tested laptops, its speed was adequate for common tasks such as web browsing, video conferencing, and application startup. Performance was okay but on the slow side when composing documents, working on data spreadsheets, and running other productivity tasks, and it was slow for manipulating images, editing videos, and calculating simulations.

Portability: This laptop is a Good choice for traveling, although not ideal. Battery life lasted 11.75 hours in a light load of web browsing tests, and 7 hours in a heavier load of 4K video playback tests. Results could get you through a typical workday, under a workload of mixed use. At 3.3 lbs, weight was typical for a laptop of this size category.

Ergonomics: Some features of the keyboard, touchpad, and labeling, were well-designed, and were comfortable or convenient to use. The keyboard has large keys and was comfortably sized. Its high contrast letters were easy to read, and the backlighting can be useful in dark rooms. The power button was well-labeled, but it was inconveniently placed, either difficult to reach or too easy to accidentally press. A stylus is included for use with the touch screen. The keyboard can be folded away, allowing the screen to be used like a tablet. The touchscreen is smooth enough for fast swipes, and fingerprints clean off easily. Testers liked the sturdy build of the chassis.

Display: The display quality was Very Good overall. Colors were in the ballpark, though not completely accurate. The display has a wide viewing angle, especially important if more than one person needs to see the screen at a time, say, for a video or presentation. Its display produces a smaller array of colors than on most other tested laptops.

Useful features and attributes on this model include: Laptop converts to a touchscreen tablet to be used as either a laptop computer or a tablet. The 256GB solid-state drive uses less power and accesses data more quickly than conventional hard-disk drives. You can connect common external devices such as hard drives and Blu-ray burners using Thunderbolt 3 (40 Gbps) for maximum performance. The fingerprint reader lets you log into your computer without typing in a password. This laptop has a full-size HDMI port and supports DisplayPort over USB-C for connecting to an HDTV or monitor.

Downsides: There's no optical drive like a CD or DVD reader, so you'll have to buy an external drive if you need one.

expertReview.summary: A 14.0-inch convertible laptop tested with Windows 11 Home, an Intel Core i5-1235U 1.3GHz processor, 8GB of memory, Intel Iris Xe Graphics graphics, a touchscreen, and a 512GB solid-state drive.
expertReview.bottomLine: The IPS touch display of the Acer Spin 3 SP314-55N-53GS laptop has better contrast and near accurate color but a slightly yellow skin tone than other tested laptops. Its convertible form factor gives it the flexibility to switch between laptop and tablet modes; plus, the touchscreen is a convenient way to navigate, especially if you're away from a standard desk during travels. Its battery life results for web browsing of 13.75 hours is average but above average for the 10.0 hours of video playback for its size category. This laptop is Very Good for intensive computational tasks, but you may notice a slowdown when running more demanding graphical tasks.
expertReview.highs:
• Shows fast speeds in our performance tests
• Touchscreen provides a convenient way to navigate and interact
• Long battery life could last beyond a full day's work
• Comes with a large amount of total storage space
• Comes with a fast, more efficient solid-state drive
• Has a fingerprint reader
expertReview.lows: • No optical drive
expertReview.description:
The Acer Spin 3 SP314-55N-53GS is a 14-inch convertible laptop with a screen resolution of 1920 x 1080. It has 8GB of memory and a 512GB solid-state drive. It has an Intel Core i5-1235U 1.3GHz processor and an integrated Intel Iris Xe Graphics. It lacks an optical drive for burning CDs or DVDs. It was tested with Windows 11 Home installed.

It has a touch screen, 2 full-size, 2 type-C USB ports built-in on the laptop. However, you'll lose a USB port to plug in the power cable when charging the laptop. Video outputs include: an HDMI full-size port, supporting Thunderbolt 4 (40 Gbps) and DisplayPort over USB-C. It supports WiFi 5 (802.11ac), so it's compatible with high-speed routers. It also supports WiFi 6 (802.11ax), which provides faster and more dependable High Efficiency Wireless, but you'll need a compatible router to see the faster speeds. It has Bluetooth 5.0 built-in. It has a 0.9MP webcam for video conferencing. It has a stylus with a built-in holder.

The Acer Spin 3 SP314-55N-53GS measures 12.6 inches wide by 8.2 inches deep by 0.9 inches high, and it weighs 3.2 lbs. It's backed by a 12-month warranty, with 12 months of free tech support over telephone.
expertReview.review:
Performance: Overall this laptop's performance was Very Good. Tasks like email, word processing and web browsing will be accomplished quickly. Compared to other tested laptops, it was among the fastest with common tasks such as web browsing and video conferencing. Applications start up almost instantly. It was fast when composing documents with images, calculating large data spreadsheets, and running other productivity tasks, and it was slow for manipulating images, editing videos, and calculating simulations. Its playback was smoother than most other tested laptops, even when video game settings were maxed out.

Portability: This laptop is a Very Good choice for traveling. Battery life lasted 13.75 hours in a light load of web browsing tests, and 10 hours in a heavier load of 4K video playback tests. Results were notably longer than many similar laptops, under a workload of mixed use. At 3.2 lbs, weight was typical for a laptop of this size category.

Ergonomics: The laptop features, such as its keyboard, touchpad, and labeling were well-designed, making it comfortable and convenient to use. The keyboard has large keys and was comfortably sized. Its high contrast letters were easy to read, and the backlighting can be useful in dark rooms. The power button was well labeled and conveniently located. A stylus is included for use with the touch screen. The keyboard can be folded away, allowing the screen to be used like a tablet. The touchscreen is smooth enough for fast swipes, and fingerprints clean off easily. Testers like the sturdy build of the chassis.

Display: The display quality was Very Good overall. Colors were accurately reproduced, realistic, and natural looking. The display was highly prone to glare making it difficult to see in a brightly lit room or outdoors. The display has a wide viewing angle, especially important if more than one person needs to see the screen at a time, say, for a video or presentation. Its display has better contrast than on most other tested laptops.

Useful features and attributes on this model include: Laptop converts to a touchscreen tablet to be used as either a laptop computer or a tablet. The 512GB solid-state drive uses less power and accesses data more quickly than conventional hard-disk drives. You can connect common external devices such as hard drives and Blu-ray burners using Thunderbolt 4 (40 Gbps) for maximum performance. The fingerprint reader lets you log into your computer without typing in a password. This laptop has a full-size HDMI port and supports DisplayPort over USB-C for connecting to an HDTV or monitor.

Downsides: There's no optical drive like a CD or DVD reader, so you'll have to buy an external drive if you need one. At about 6 ft length, the power cable is shorter than most others, so you'd need to be mindful of power outlet locations.

expertReview.description:
The Acer Swift 3 SF314-43-R6NE (AMD Ryzen) is a 14-inch laptop with a screen resolution of 1920 x 1080. It has 16GB of memory and a 512GB solid-state drive. It has an AMD Ryzen 7 5700U 1.8GHz processor and an integrated AMD Radeon Graphics. It lacks an optical drive for burning CDs or DVDs. It was tested with Windows 11 Home installed.

It has 2 full-size, 1 type-C USB ports built-in on the laptop. Video outputs include: an HDMI full-size port, supporting DisplayPort over USB-C. It supports WiFi 5 (802.11ac), so it's compatible with high-speed routers. It also supports WiFi 6 (802.11ax), which provides faster and more dependable High Efficiency Wireless, but you'll need a compatible router to see the faster speeds. It has Bluetooth 5.2 built-in. It has a 0.9MP webcam for video conferencing.

The Acer Swift 3 SF314-43-R6NE (AMD Ryzen) measures 12.7 inches wide by 8.5 inches deep by 0.8 inches high, and it weighs 2.9 lbs. It's backed by a 12-month warranty, with 12 months of free tech support over telephone.
expertReview.review:
Performance: Overall this laptop's performance was Good, below that of many other models but still powerful enough for tasks such as email, word processing, web browsing, and streaming movies. Compared to other tested laptops, its speed was adequate for common tasks such as web browsing, video conferencing, and application startup. Speed was adequate when composing documents, working on data spreadsheets, and other productivity tasks, and it was slow for manipulating images, editing videos, and calculating simulations.

Portability: This laptop is a Very Good choice for traveling. Battery life lasted 14.5 hours in a light load of web browsing tests, and 9.75 hours in a heavier load of 4K video playback tests. Results were notably longer than many similar laptops, under a workload of mixed use. At 2.9 lbs, weight was typical for a laptop of this size category.

Ergonomics: Some features of the keyboard, touchpad, and labeling, were well-designed, and were comfortable or convenient to use. The keyboard has large keys and was comfortably sized. Its high contrast letters were easy to read, and the backlighting can be useful in dark rooms. The power button was well labeled and conveniently located.

Display: The display quality was Very Good overall. Colors were in the ballpark, though not completely accurate. The display was anti-reflective, so there was little or no glare when viewing in a brightly lit room or outdoors. The display has a wide viewing angle, especially important if more than one person needs to see the screen at a time, say, for a video or presentation. Its display produces a smaller array of colors than on most other tested laptops.

Useful features and attributes on this model include: The 512GB solid-state drive uses less power and accesses data more quickly than conventional hard-disk drives. You can connect common external devices such as hard drives and Blu-ray burners using USB 3.2 Gen 1 (5 Gbps) for maximum performance. The fingerprint reader lets you log into your computer without typing in a password. This laptop has a full-size HDMI port and supports DisplayPort over USB-C for connecting to an HDTV or monitor.

Downsides: There's no optical drive like a CD or DVD reader, so you'll have to buy an external drive if you need one. There is no memory-card reader, so you'll need to buy an external reader or connect your digital camera directly to this laptop to transfer photos.

expertReview.summary: The Aeotec Cam 360 has 1080p video resolution, and has Excellent 360 degree field of view.
expertReview.bottomLine: The Aeotec Cam 360 has 1080p video resolution. Overall this model has Very Good video with higher quality detail than many, Very Good data security offering a high level of protection from your data being hacked or stolen, responds quickly to be able to speak with a visitor and has and two-way audio communication. It uses SmartThings as a digital assistant that can be used with your voice to view video from the doorbell.
expertReview.highs:
• Very Good job for video quality
  • Very Good response time (a score based on elapsed time between motion occuring within the cameras field of view and the ability to speak to the visitor)
  • Excellent 360 degree field of view

expertReview.summary: Portable bluetooth wireless open bone conduction earphones that come with USB charging cable, ear plugs, carrying bag.
expertReview.bottomLine: This wireless Bluetooth model from AfterShokz delivers fair sound quality; while casual listeners may find it adequate for movie and TV dialog and communications it's not a good choice for those whose focus is music. It features a unique, bone-conduction design - the speaker drivers are placed on either side of the head forward of the ears rather than over or in the ears like with traditional headphones. The concept is that stereo sound can be delivered to the inner ears via the listener's cheekbones rather than through the eardrums. Since the drivers don't block the ear canal, they don't muffle external noise, and some sound from the drivers will escape. As such, they are best suited for those who listen in quiet environments where disturbing others is not an issue, or for those who want to be able to hear what's going on around them while they use the headphones.
expertReview.description: The AfterShokz OpenMove portable Bluetooth wireless earphones have a open bone conduction design. These iPod/cellphone-centric earphones are intended for use with iPods, iPads, some other cell phones, as well as standard audio devices, and have a claimed reception range of around 33 feet and are intended for use with Bluetooth enabled audio devices including cell phones, as well as standard audio devices. The earphones have an inline microphone and inline remote with and integrated volume, music player function, and call connect/disconnect controls. Additional features include Has 3 EQ settings. Manufacturer claims dust and water resistance (IP55). It has power on/off and Bluetooth connect, EQ setting, and battery status voice announcements, and control actuation and Bluetooth disconnect alert tones. Supports digital voice assistants when used with Bluetooth connected devices that have those features. Bluetooth connected Apple mobile devices using iOS Version 5 and above will show the battery level. The OpenMove comes with USB charging cable, ear plugs, carrying bag and is covered by a 24-month parts/24-month labor warranty.
expertReview.review:
Design and features:This Bluetooth wireless portable bone conduction model provides fair sound. The OpenMove has a volume control plus an integrated microphone and player function controls. Additional features include Has 3 EQ settings. Manufacturer claims dust and water resistance (IP55). It has power on/off and Bluetooth connect, EQ setting, and battery status voice announcements, and control actuation and Bluetooth disconnect alert tones. Supports compatible digital voice assistants when used with Bluetooth connected devices that have those features. Bluetooth connected Apple mobile devices using iOS Version 5 and above will show the battery level. This model comes with USB-A to USB-C charging cable, ear plugs, carrying bag.

Sound quality: We found the OpenMove delivers sound quality that falls in the fair range - meaning that it has sonic shortcomings that leave a lot to be desired when listening to music but don't rule it out for dialog and communication. This model has three tone settings; the standard tone setting was used. What little bass (as in bass drums, bass guitars, stand-up bass, etc.) it had was very subdued and lacked impact and depth. The midrange (voices, guitars, horns, etc.) was hazy, congested, somewhat thin and a bit nasal. The treble (cymbals, the upper range of violins, etc.) was fairly extended, but subdued and a bit sizzly (sounds that should have a delicate shimmer have a sound reminiscent of bacon frying). Does a so-so job of recovering midrange tonal region room ambience from recordings. It has an open sound, but that's because it's not covering your ears, not because the audio sounds open and it the sound lacks liveliness. Neutral character. The overall sound can be summarized as telephone-like. The other tone setting had a noticeable effect on the sound; in the voice booster mode the vocal range was a bit more prominent, and in the earplug mode when the provided earplugs were used and a good seal was achieved the sound became a bit distant and echoey.

Comfort: We found that these earphones produce a slight sense of pressure in front of the ears. It fits securely even with vigorous head movement. When played at its loudest volume (which is not very loud) a vibration can be felt that might feel like an electric shock (but it's not). The neckband is generally not noticeable unless it interferes with clothing, hair, headwear, or you have a really large head.

attributes.name: Sound quality
attributes.description: Represents the tonal accuracy, clarity, detail, ambience, and dynamics of the audio reproduced by the headphones.

attributes.name: Sensitivity
attributes.description: An assessment of how loud wire connected headphones will play for a given audio input signal level. This is an important consideration if the headphones will be used with audio devices that have relatively low maximum audio output signal levels like some battery powered portables. Some models may have 2 sensitivity levels given: one with the highest selectable setting and the other with the lowest selectable setting. Not applicable for wireless headphones that do not have a cord connected option.

attributes.name: Type
attributes.description: Over the ear models completely envelop the ear. On-ear models sit on top of the ears. Insert models are inserted into the ear canal. Earbud models rest in the ear outside of the ear canal and may have a portion that extends into the ear canal.

attributes.name: Design
attributes.description: Closed headphones rest on or around the user's ears and rely on a seal between the user's ears and the headphone for proper bass response, and somewhat isolate the user from outside sounds.  Open air models rest on or around the user's ears but do not rely on a seal between the user's ears and headphones for proper bass response and do not isolate the user from outside sounds. Ear insert models are inserted into and are held in place by the ear canal; they rely on a seal between the user's ears and the headphones for proper bass response, and somewhat isolate the user from outside sounds. Earbud models rest in the area outside of the ear canal and may extend into the ear canal but do not rely on the ear canal to be held in place; they do not rely on a seal between the user's ears and headphones for proper bass response and do not isolate the user from outside sounds.

attributes.name: Sports model

expertReview.summary: This Air Innovations humidifier was excellent in overall performance, and is intended to humidify areas up to 178 square feet.
expertReview.bottomLine: This highly rated humidifier has several features not often found on small-room models. It’s programable and comes with a built-in humidistat, which measures a room’s relative humidity (though in CR tests, the sensor’s performance was just average). The moisture output, energy efficiency, and noise levels are all rated Excellent. Convenience is also impressive, though cleaning may be a challenge because most hands won’t fit inside the water tank.
expertReview.highs:
• Claims to inhibit microbes.
  • Programmable
  • Indicator for empty tank
  • Automatic shut-off when empty
  • It comes with a humidistat to control the humidity level
  • Is equipped with a digital humidity display
expertReview.lows: This model had no discernible flaws in its performance.

If you're looking for information about blenders, Consumer Reports is your best resource. Consumer Reports’ blender reviews will give you honest buying advice that you can trust. test_endpoint.productGroupIntroText: Make quality shakes, soups, smoothies, and frozen drinks with a versatile blender. The blender that's right for you—from personal to high-performance—depends on what you're making.
test_endpoint.buyingGuideIntroText: The first blenders hit kitchen counters in the 1920s, designed for whipping up malted milks. Today, they’re more versatile—and they’re the best tool for making tasty smoothies, succulent soups, even homemade nut butters. You can get a plastic personal blender for as little as $20 or splurge on a multifunction, premium glass blender with Bluetooth that will cost more than $600.Higher price... typically means better functionality, versatility, and performance. Still, results are, well, mixed. Some blender blades broke under our rigorous durability tests using only ice. Others blended perfect virgin piña coladas. Our buying guide will steer you toward the best blender for your needs and budget.

expertReviews.bestVersionsToGet: Any Boxster is fun. We'd stick with a manual transmission, even though Porsche's PDK automated manual is rather good. Careful with the options, because they quickly boost the sticker price. Special ordering your car from the dealer might help control the sticker shock.
expertReviews.comfortAndconvenience:
Driving position

The Boxster is well set up for enthusiastic driving, with controls within easy reach and adequate if not generous room all around. The power tilt and telescope steering wheel has a good adjustment range, and the shifter is close at hand. Leg and head room are adequate for taller drivers, but some shorter drivers had trouble getting close enough to fully depress the clutch. The driving space is narrow, and the center console and left wheel well intrudes somewhat.

Visibility

The low seating position, high dashboard and rear deck can make rear visibility difficult especially for smaller drivers. But thin front pillars and good sized windows make for adequate visibility to the front and sides. The sides of the fabric roof create large blind spots when it is up, but even with the top down the screened wind blocker, high rear trunk deck, and roll hoops impede the view to the rear. A rear-view camera is optional for 2015.

Seat comfort and access

Seats are very firm and supportive, with aggressive backrest bolstering that holds you in place in corners, but only if you fit. Some drivers of average size found the narrow seats confining. An adjustable lumbar support helps with lower-back support, and a power adjustment for bottom cushion length adds thigh support. Optional cooled seats on our car struggled to keep you cool in hot weather but work better in more moderate conditions.

Controls and gauges

A large and legible analog tachometer sits front and center in the instrument display, and contains an easy to read digital speedometer. A smaller and harder to read 190 mph analog speedometer sits to the left. Other information including fuel, audio, and optional navigation is contained in a very clear and easy to use digital display. Like other Porsches, the center console is cluttered with a lot of small buttons packed closely together, a design that can make operating things confusing and distracting when underway. A well-designed touch screen is easy to read and use for other functions including radio preset selection, but the audio system lacks a tuning knob. Our car has no steering wheel mounted audio controls -- an annoying omission in a $60,000 car. Other quirks include the traditional Porsche left-hand ignition switch, a dashboard mounted door lock button, and the lack of a standard USB port. But Bluetooth phone pairing was straightforward and worked well in our Boxster.

Interior fit and finish

The cabin is finished with quality materials, and padded surfaces that are soft to the touch. The partial leather seats are neatly finished, and the carpet is high quality. But we found some poor fits and uneven gaps, and the cup holders that pop out of the dashboard feel like flimsy afterthoughts.

Convertible top operation

The lined fabric top operates very quickly with the press of a single button, going up or down in only about ten seconds. It can be raised and lowered at speeds up to 30 mph, which allows for more impulsive open-air motoring. Putting the top down doesn't encroach on luggage space, a downfall of many other convertibles. A netting windblocker helps keep the cabin calm when the top is down.

Cabin storage and cargo room

The front trunk is large enough to swallow up a large upright suitcase, and the rear trunk can handle a couple of duffels or a set of golf clubs. But neither trunk can be locked to prevent access from the cabin. If a thief can get in the car, they can pull the release and get into your trunk. The Boxster doesn't come with a spare tire, just a bottle of sealer and an air compressor.
expertReviews.modelYearSummaryLong: Porsche's entry-level roadster is tremendous fun to drive and offers strong performance. Both the base and S versions are offered with a choice of a six-speed manual or a seven-speed automated-manual transmission. The base model we tested had a responsive six-cylinder engine and a smooth, crisp-shifting manual transmission. Handling is still excellent despite some loss of steering feedback in the current generation, and the ride is not punishing. The power top deploys quickly and can be operated at speeds up to 35 mph, and the front and rear trunks are a bonus. Reliability has been average. The 2017 model year brings a new name "718 Boxster" and new 2.0- and 2.5-liter turbocharged four-cylinder engines.
expertReviews.modelYearSummaryShort: The Boxster's 2.7-liter six-cylinder is very responsive and the six-speed manual shifter is smooth and crisp. Handling is still excellent despite some loss of steering feedback and the ride is not punishing. It's a tremendous car to drive, and the S version is even more powerful. A seven-speed automatic is optional.
expertReviews.nutshellOverview:
This two-seat mid-engined roadster has become an instant favorite at our test track, thanks to excellent handling, braking, and quick, direct steering. With its 2013 redesign, the Boxster gets shapely new sheet metal to go with its quick reflexes, well-finished interior and responsive powertrain. It's also more livable for the everyday grind than ever before, including a tolerable ride and one of the slickest operating convertible tops in the business.

But while it may be more affordable than Porsche's flagship sports car, the 911, the Boxster is far from an entry-level offering. Prices start at $49,500, and as is typical for Porsche, the price climbs quickly with options. Our base model with a manual transmission and a few extras rang in at $59,600 -- and our car was relatively lightly-optioned.

Our test car is powered by a 265-hp, 2.7-liter flat six-cylinder engine paired with a six-speed manual transmission that provides quick acceleration, an exhilarating exhaustsoundtrack, and 23-mpg overall. A seven-speed automated manual transmission is also available, as is an S model with a a 315-hp, 3.4-liter six-cylinder for buyers in need of more grunt. Either way, the mid-engine design allows for trunks front and rear, which add a measure of practicality.

As much fun as the Boxster is to drive, we can't overlook some gripes. The well-contoured sports seats provide great support, but many will find them too narrow. Typical Porsche controls mean the console is cluttered with small buttons. And rear visibility out of the raised top is tough.

A rear-view camera is optional for 2015.
expertReviews.performance:
Handling This is where the Boxster shines, with agile handling that makes it fun to drive from the first corner regardless of speed. The Boxster turns in quickly, with immediate response and lots of grip. Body lean is virtually non existent, and the steering is quick and well-weighted with excellent feedback, although the redesign brings a change from hydraulic to electric power steering. There is less steering feel than before, but only Porsche purists will likely notice the difference. At the track, the Boxster nailed our avoidance maneuver, snaking through the cones at 58 mph while instilling plenty of driver confidence. It showed a lot of grip at speed, with gradual and predictable breakaway at the limit. A sport mode slackens the stability control settings and allows for some rear end slide.

Powertrain With the base 265-hp, 2.7-liter six-cylinder engine and six-speed manual transmission, our Boxster provides quick acceleration, but is slower than competing sports cars including the four-cylinder BMW Z4. There isn't a whole lot of torque either, so you have to wind the engine out to get the most out of it. This is no hardship as the 2.7-liter six-cylinder revs smoothly and easily, and sounds terrific as engine speed increases. Engine speeds over 4000 rpm emit a glorious wail.

Transmission ratios are well-suited to the engine, and the shifter is precise with low effort, but the shift lever feels oddly too long. Some drivers found the clutch effort heavy. We recorded a 0-60 acceleration time of 6.1 seconds and 23-mpg overall on required premium fuel. An automatic start/stop system shuts off and restarts the engine to save fuel. For drivers who prefer to let the car do the shifting,a slick-shifting seven-speed automated manual PDK transmission is available for another $3200.

Braking The Boxster's brakes are among the best we've tested, with short stops in wet or dry conditions and a responsive pedal even after repeated hard stops.

Ride comfort and noise The ride is firm and well controlled, but impacts are nicely muted overall. The Boxster is very civilized around town and on the highway, especially for a car with 20-inch tires. With the engine located right behind the driver's head, engine noise is noticeable, but in a good way. A smooth mechanical hum and mellow exhaust note become louder under full throtttle, but it's not a sound enthusiast drivers will find objectionable. Wind and road noise are noticeable in moderate driving even with the top up, but conversation is possible underway with the top up or down thanks, in part to the screened wind blocker behind the seats.

Headlights Excellent intensity but only fair distance from low beams. High beams also have excellent intensity and reach a very good distance.
expertReviews.safetyRemarks:
Safety belts

The belts are equipped with pretensioners and force limiters to reduce belt slack and forces in the event of a crash.

Air bags Front air bags, seatback-mounted side-impact air bags, and curtain head-protection air bags are standard.

Head restraints These are non-adjustable, but tall enough to provide protection for most.

Crash-avoidance systems Standard equipment includes stability control, traction control, brake assist, and antilock brakes.

Driving with kids The Boxster has no LATCH anchors or top-tethers, but front- and rear-facing seats should prove secure with safety belts. That said, two-seaters are never the best choice for transporting children, who are always safer in a rear seat.

expertReviews.makeSummary: For decades, the iconic 911 has been the symbol of what makes a Porsche. While sporty models such as the Boxster roadster and Cayman two-door coupe brought the Porsche mystique to those with slightly smaller budgets, the product line expanded to include two SUVs and two luxury four-door sedans. The Porsche DNA is still baked into every model with sharp handling, a controlled ride, superb braking performance, a thrilling exhaust note, and beautifully crafted interiors. Fuel-efficient hybrid and plug-in hybrid versions of the SUVs are available, as well. The all-electric Taycan sedan is a serious challenger to Tesla’s Model S.

expertReviews.safetyRemark: ABS and side air bags standard. ESC available from 2001, standard from 2005. Head protection air bags standard from 2005.
expertReviews.usedModelSummary: This sporty mid-engine roadster has fun, agile handling, excellent brakes, and precise steering. The ride is firm and well controlled, yet not punishing. The two fore-and-aft trunks add some practicality. The power top is easy to operate and works at up to 30 mph. 2007 brought styling updates and power upgrades, as well as six-speed gearboxes. In 2009 the Boxsters gained a seven-speed sequential transmission. An all-new Boxster arrived for 2013 with a longer wheelbase and a wider track. Handling is excellent even with the electric steering, and the ride is not punishing. Interior quality and refinement were improved. For 2017, Porsche's redesigned Boxster roadster was named 718 Boxster. It came with turbocharged 2.0- and 2.5-liter four-cylinder engines, replacing the previous Sixes, but retained the impressive grip and balance.

modelGeneration.modelGenerationSummary: An all-new Boxster arrived for 2013, with all of the attributes we loved about previous models, as well as a longer wheelbase, more power and a wider track. A seven-speed automated manual transmission is offered alongside the traditional six-speed manual. Handling is excellent, even with the electric steering and the ride is not punishing. Interior quality and refinement were improved. Standard safety equipment includes stability control, traction control, brake assist, and antilock brakes.
